name: workstation-32c
description: Hypothetical two-die workstation NPU: two client-16c dies sharing one DRAM, 32 cores, the core count of the 32-core Neural Engine Apple states for M3 Ultra together with over 800GB/s of memory bandwidth (no operations-per-second figure stated). 32 cores of 32x32 output-stationary arrays: 32768 MAC/cycle, 78.6432 TOP/s at 1.2 GHz and 2 ops/MAC. DRAM 667 B/cycle, the smallest integer rate that reaches 800 GB/s at 1.2 GHz (800.4 GB/s), shared with the CPU and GPU; no die-to-die link is modeled. Every per-core parameter is client-16c's: SRAM 256 KiB (the S10 rule over both points), one 256-bit AXI port (32 read channels of 32 B/cycle against 667 B/cycle of DRAM), Vela 5.2.0 Ethos-U85 DRAM latencies and outstanding limits, 8-beat bursts, tiles 64x64x256 and an 89600 B weight cache, and the depthwise datapath 128 MAC/cycle, which the S9 rule picks on this point too. Partition auto. Pipeline 4 cycles per panel, the simulator default.
